profile.name: H3ddle

ai_relevance.text: Native Metal inference generates video, images, music, sound effects and reference-conditioned speech, then combines them on a small local timeline.

profile.maturity: Development macOS generative-media studio

novelty.text: First detailed guide in this library; documentation checked today. Repository created 2026-08-13; current source metadata is a discovery signal, not evidence of a significant product upgrade.

introduction.text: A native Apple Silicon generative-media studio combining local Metal inference with a small text, visual and audio timeline.

good_for.text: Draft an atmospheric short by generating stills, video, ambience and narration, then arrange them in one Mac project.

demo.text: The repository describes the studio and downloadable development builds; its model picker is the local starting point.

installation.text: Documentation-based setup route; commands are examples from the project and were not executed during this review.
steps: Download the macOS development release, or clone the repository for an Xcode build.
For a source build, generate the project and open it in Xcode; install a selected model through the app.

usage.text: Begin with a small, permitted sample and inspect the result.
steps: Select an installed model and set prompt, duration and canvas.
Queue a short generation, inspect the result and add it to the timeline.
Save the project and export through the documented system media frameworks.

requirements.text: Published requirements and explicit documentation gaps follow.
requirements.hardware: Apple Silicon is required. The README discusses weight streaming on 16/32 GB Macs, but does not establish a universal minimum RAM or total storage requirement.
requirements.software: macOS >=15; source builds require Xcode >=26 and XcodeGen >=2.46. FFmpeg/FFprobe are optional fallbacks for containers unsupported by system frameworks.
requirements.platforms: Native macOS Apple Silicon only in the documented route; no Intel Mac, Windows or Linux build is claimed.

license.text: The complete top-level Apache-2.0 software terms were reviewed and archived today; model/dependency/host terms remain separate.
license.weights: Weights are separately downloaded and licensed. YuE2-3B is explicitly CC-BY-NC 4.0; MiniMax H3, LTX and other checkpoints require independent terms review.
license.commercial: The main Apache-2.0 code grant permits commercial use under its notice/source and other conditions. Model, component, asset and hosted-service permission is separate. Weights are separately downloaded and licensed. YuE2-3B is explicitly CC-BY-NC 4.0; MiniMax H3, LTX and other checkpoints require independent terms review.
license.cost: Local inference avoids a required paid API, but compute and model-specific permissions remain separate from Apache-2.0 app code.

quality.text: Assessment: a native local generation queue and saved recipes are promising for Mac experimentation. The README distinguishes measured short runs from projected long-video speeds; neither was reproduced here.

limitations.text: The timeline is deliberately small. Some model paths are experimental; engineering speed projections are not completed benchmarks or guarantees.

profile.maturity: Research prototype

novelty.text: First detailed library baseline. Documentation and complete software license checked on 2026-10-07; no claim of a new release today.

introduction.text: A SIGGRAPH Asia 2021 implementation of learned wave propagation for holographic AR/VR display research.

good_for.text: Generating SLM phase patterns from RGB/RGB-D targets and calibrating multi-plane holographic displays.

demo.text: The official project presents video, AR/VR prototype results and research comparisons.

installation.text: Documented setup guidance; these commands were not executed during this review.
steps: Clone the project and create its neural3d Conda environment.
For physical work, install compatible camera/SLM SDKs and adjust optical parameters to the real setup.
Begin with the supplied simulation/phase-generation example before camera-in-the-loop calibration.

usage.text: Begin with a small example and inspect the result before using it in production.
steps: Inspect the generated phase and simulated reconstruction.
If using physical equipment, follow per-plane homography calibration and training instructions; repeat with the actual optical parameters.

requirements.text: Source-backed requirements; unreported minimums remain unknown.
requirements.hardware: Physical work needs an SLM, camera and optical illumination system. Numeric RAM/VRAM minima are not documented; optional released training datasets are approximately 60 GB or 220 GB.
requirements.software: PyTorch >=1.10 with complex operations, PyTorch Lightning and env.yml dependencies. PyCapture2 and HOLOEYE SDK or slmPy are documented hardware routes.
requirements.platforms: Research Python/optics workflow; a complete desktop-OS support matrix is not stated. Not a plug-in for ordinary consumer headsets.

license.text: The complete top-level MIT software license was reviewed and archived. Dependent models and components retain their own terms.
license.weights: MIT source for this 3D implementation. Vendor SDKs, datasets and trained assets have independent terms; the older 2020 Neural Holography repository has different licensing.
license.commercial: The reviewed software license permits commercial software use subject to its obligations; it does not clear independent weights, data, assets, services or dependencies.
license.cost: Source code is available under the stated license. Compute, storage, optional hardware and any hosted model/API services can add costs; no current service-price quote is asserted.

quality.text: Included for its concrete documented creative workflow: Generating SLM phase patterns from RGB/RGB-D targets and calibrating multi-plane holographic displays. The documentation and developer examples support relevance; output quality, setup success and performance were not independently tested.

limitations.text: Specialist calibration is central to reproduction. Project comparisons are author experiments, and the site notes limits in its DPAC comparison. No optical apparatus was installed or tested.

quality_assessment.scope: Generating SLM phase patterns from RGB/RGB-D targets and calibrating multi-plane holographic displays.
caveats: Source review only; AI Media Scout did not install, execute or benchmark this application.

steps: Download the open-source Electron release for your platform from the official GitHub release page.

steps: Use a built-in voice or a clean reference recording you have permission to use.

requirements.text: Requirements are source-specific. Unreported capacities and untested platforms are not inferred.

requirements.software: Packaged Electron app with managed Python/PyTorch backend and downloaded models. Source development requires Node 22+, Bun, Rust/Cargo and build tools.
requirements.platforms: NVIDIA CUDA on Windows/Linux; Apple Silicon MPS; slower CPU routes. Intel Mac is UI plus remote backend. Windows ARM is experimental and the website/README differ on native packaging, so verify the exact release asset.

quality.text: Explicit engine/device reporting and platform documentation help choose a realistic local workflow.

limitations.text: The current release notes describe unsigned/ad-hoc-signed, non-notarized installers and manual Mac updates. Quality and memory vary by engine. profile.name: Shodō — Ink & Gesture

ai_relevance.text: An experimental calligraphy workbench where an AI proposes ordered brush gestures, an SVG renderer paints them and the user edits each stroke. Vision can critique selected characters against a reference. Creative use: Making editable calligraphic studies and expressive lettering, then refining paths, pressure, brush texture and multi-character composition before SVG or PNG export.

profile.maturity: Experimental creative prototype

novelty.text: First detailed guide in this library. The repository was created in the current discovery window; this is a documentation baseline, not a verified launch date.

introduction.text: An experimental calligraphy workbench where an AI proposes ordered brush gestures, an SVG renderer paints them and the user edits each stroke. Vision can critique selected characters against a reference.

good_for.text: Making editable calligraphic studies and expressive lettering, then refining paths, pressure, brush texture and multi-character composition before SVG or PNG export.

demo.text: Recorded AI studies for 愛 and 森羅万象 are included and can be edited without a new API request. The hosted prototype is private, and the repository contains a demo script rather than a finished demo video.

installation.text: Follow the reviewed project route below; these steps are documentation guidance and were not executed.
steps: Install Node.js 22.13+ and npm, clone the official repository and install its locked dependencies with npm ci.
Start the local development server with npm run dev and open localhost:5180.
For new AI generation, copy the example environment file to the ignored local environment file and configure the provider key. Prepared/recorded studies work without a key.

usage.text: A small first project that exercises the documented creative workflow.
steps: Open a recorded study, select a stroke and change a curve handle or pressure point.
For a new work, enter a short phrase and inspect character identity/order before accepting an optional critique.
Arrange the composition and export SVG/PNG plus Study JSON to preserve editable paths and brush settings.

requirements.software: Node.js 22.13+, npm and a desktop browser. Windows ARM64 needs x64 Node for the documented Worker runtime. New generations require network access and a configured provider account.
requirements.platforms: Desktop-oriented web application; Windows ARM64 setup is described. General macOS/Linux compatibility and mobile support were not independently established from the reviewed documentation.

license.commercial: The reviewed MIT software license permits commercial use subject to its license, notice and source-sharing obligations where applicable. This does not establish permission for every model, input, output or service.
license.cost: Recorded studies and editing need no model account. New generation and vision critique may incur provider charges.

quality.text: The output is editable vector geometry, and the documentation distinguishes generated studies from deterministic prepared paths and acknowledges character/style limits.

limitations.text: Hackathon prototype: approximate procedural brush rendering, subjective AI critiques, no guaranteed stroke-order correctness, and no typographic kerning for Latin text. Uploaded visual references are sent with generation; no external artwork was submitted in this review. This edition is a documentation review, not an installation or output-quality test.

introduction.text: An agent plug-in and local MCP toolkit for building and inspecting Blender models, scenes and animation, retaining both the editable blend file and the Python construction source.

good_for.text: Creating controlled props and scene prototypes from a brief, comparing reference silhouettes and revising geometry with repeatable inspection views.

demo.text: Its primary site publishes paired scene examples and mixed technical/visual review results. The selected gallery image is not an average-quality claim, and no Blender scene was built in this review.

installation.text: Follow the reviewed project route below; these steps are documentation guidance and were not executed.
steps: Install Blender separately; the author tests Blender 5.2 LTS. Prepare Bun 1.3.5+ and a supported coding-agent host.
Use the project’s documented plug-in installer for the chosen host, then expose Blender on PATH or configure its executable location.
Start a fresh agent session and verify access using a small saved test scene. Optional scene-understanding tools require a separately built Rust runtime; the basic tools do not.

usage.text: A small first project that exercises the documented creative workflow.
steps: Provide a short prop brief with dimensions, purpose and finish goals.
Review a graybox before materials, then inspect a hero render and fixed views.
Save the blend file and Python source; for a GLB delivery, reopen the export and check what survived.

requirements.software: Blender 5.2 LTS is the author-tested version; Bun 1.3.5+; a compatible coding-agent host; Rust only for the optional scene-understanding runtime.
requirements.platforms: A Windows executable-path example is documented, but a complete tested OS/GPU matrix is not provided. Agent-host availability and Blender support must be checked separately.

quality.text: Editable scene/source delivery and explicit export reopening are useful quality controls. The author’s small paired evaluation reports mixed visual outcomes and higher token use, not universal superiority.

limitations.text: Some asset workflows are browser handoffs rather than automatic live retrieval. Scene checks and preview gates cannot guarantee artistic quality or production-ready topology. This edition is a documentation review, not an installation or output-quality test.

good_for.text: Compose short synthetic vocal phrases and edit note timing or pitch contours in a Max patch or Max for Live device, with separately permitted voice and score inputs.

demo.text: The repository links a Max interface and the original TCSinger 2 demo. Its exported checkpoint is a reproduction trained on four named singing datasets, not the official original checkpoint. Published research comparisons do not independently validate this export or its real-time reliability.

installation.text: For inference, use Apple Silicon/macOS 14+ and Max 9+ with neural.gen~ installed. Download the exported model/tokenizer files from the linked model repository into export/max, or use the device download button. Open the bundled TCSinger2_UI.amxd or Max patches. Training and re-export are separate Linux/CUDA or Mac/Python workflows; they are not needed merely to load the provided export.

usage.text: Start with a short, representative project and inspect the result before a larger batch.
steps: Open the device/patch with the exported files available to neural.gen~ and confirm both score2f0 and sing load.
Enter notes and lyrics in the piano roll or read a JSON score; set tempo explicitly before importing a score because the piano roll retains its current tempo.

Generate a short phrase, listen for pronunciation and timing errors, then edit the F0 curve and compare. More export sampling steps increase latency; do not assume a live performance deadline is guaranteed.

requirements.software: Module workers, onnxruntime-web, OpenCV.js, correctly served WASM/model assets and a compatible bundler. WebAssembly threads require SharedArrayBuffer and cross-origin isolation.
requirements.platforms: Browser WebGPU where available, WebAssembly fallback elsewhere. An Apple M-series benchmark and Node single-thread test are reported; no complete browser/OS validation matrix is supplied.

installation.text: Use the official release or build the Xcode project after retrieving its pinned MPVKit frameworks. The release is not notarized; inspect the project and release provenance before opening. Download the selected speech and translation models within the app.

introduction.text: A Chromium extension captures tab audio, transcribes with faster-whisper and overlays translated captions through a local Python backend.

steps: On the documented Windows route, create a Python virtual environment in backend and install requirements.txt.
Load extension/ through Chrome or Edge developer-mode Load unpacked.

For manual startup run python server.py in backend; the optional Native Messaging installer adds Windows auto-start. For local NLLB translation install the documented transformers, torch and sentencepiece dependencies.

usage.text: Suggested first project, using the documented controls and outputs.
steps: Play a supported non-DRM browser video.
Select source/target language, Whisper model and CPU or CUDA device, then Start.
Verify which translator is active before handling private media; Stop capture when finished.

requirements.text: Developer-documented requirements are listed separately from unreported limits.
requirements.hardware: NVIDIA GPU strongly recommended; CUDA 12 and cuDNN 9 documented. Default Whisper model about 1.6 GB; local NLLB setup about 2.5 GB additional download. RAM/VRAM minima not documented. CPU latency estimates are developer claims, not our measurements.
requirements.software: Python 3.10+, Chromium 116+, faster-whisper/FastAPI; optional NLLB/CTranslate2 dependencies. Model downloads required.
requirements.platforms: Windows 10/11 is the documented install target. README says manual backend execution is possible on Mac/Linux, but their native auto-start installers are not implemented and cross-platform behavior was not tested.

quality.text: The extension-to-local-backend design directly addresses live captions rather than only file transcription. Assessment is based on source/documentation review; runtime behavior and output quality were not tested.

limitations.text: Despite the opening offline claim, missing NLLB dependencies/model cause an automatic Google online fallback. DRM capture is unsupported; only one tab at a time. Caption/translation accuracy needs human review.

requirements.platforms: The README lists Windows 10/11, Linux and Apple Silicon macOS. This does not establish parity for every model or CUDA extension. A remote backend is documented.

good_for.text: Reviewing an edit, locating a visual or timing issue, searching spoken material and communicating a recorded interactive-art workflow to an AI assistant.

demo.text: The README supplies a storyboard/assistant-response GIF and a companion-app tour. It reports timing on an M5 Pro and explicitly says other platforms and clients have not been exercised; these are author examples, not our tests.

installation.text: Install Node 20+. Use the documented package installer scoped to the client you actually want, or register its MCP command manually. Download speech models with setup, inspect doctor output, then restart the client. The optional recorder is a separate macOS source build.

steps: Give the configured assistant the path of a short local video and request a storyboard plus a timestamped transcript.
Check the source playback; use zoom on a narrow interval and frame/crop to investigate detail that sparse storyboards miss.
Correct transcript errors and avoid treating approximate word times as frame-accurate editing marks.
If using WatchRecorder, deliberately grant screen/microphone permissions and inspect the recording before handing its frames and transcript to an AI client.

requirements.hardware: Initial speech downloads are about 0.9 MB for VAD plus 574 MB on Apple Silicon or 148 MB elsewhere. Minimum RAM/VRAM and total storage are not documented. Companion recordings and cached images/transcripts add storage.

requirements.platforms: Author tested macOS 26 on Apple Silicon through Claude Code. Linux, Windows, Intel Macs and other named MCP clients are anticipated but explicitly untested. WatchRecorder is Mac-only.

usage.text: Recording guitar with a continuous clean-to-lead tone change, or automating amp character in a DAW without changing presets.
